title: Chermoula Fish
subtitle: Grilled fish with North African herb and spice marinade
excerpt: Chermoula is a Moroccan and Tunisian herb marinade used on fish. It combines fresh herbs, garlic, cumin, and paprika into a paste that is rubbed onto the fish before grilling or pan-frying. The result is a vibrant, punchy crust that complements white fish perfectly.
sourceNotes: Chermoula is a cornerstone marinade of Moroccan and Tunisian cooking. It is used on fish, seafood, and vegetables. The spice balance and herb ratio vary by region -- some versions include preserved lemon, others add more coriander leaf.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chermoula can be made 3 days ahead and stored in the fridge. The marinated fish can be kept for up to 4 hours before cooking.

content.text: Pat the fish fillets dry before applying the chermoula. The marinade sticks better and the fish browns more evenly in the pan. A thick fillet of cod or haddock works best -- it holds together on the heat without breaking apart.
Combine the garlic, lemon juice, and olive oil in a bowl. Add the parsley, cumin, coriander, paprika, chilli flakes, and salt. Stir to make the chermoula.
Pat the fish fillets completely dry. Coat each fillet thickly with the chermoula on both sides.
Leave to marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes, or in the fridge for up to 4 hours.
Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat. No extra oil is needed -- the chermoula has enough.
Cook the fish for 3 to 4 minutes per side until the chermoula is lightly charred at the edges and the fish is cooked through.
Serve with a wedge of lemon, flatbread, and a simple salad or roasted vegetables.

items.symptom: Chermoula is burning before fish is cooked
items.fix: Reduce heat to medium and finish the fish gently; the herbs can catch quickly over high heat

items.symptom: Fish is sticking to the pan
items.cause: Pan not hot enough before adding the fish
items.fix: Let the pan get properly hot before placing the fish, skin-side down; it will release when ready

items.cause: Fish was not dry before marinating
items.fix: Pat the fish completely dry with kitchen paper before applying the chermoula

content.text: Chermoula is used across Morocco, Tunisia, and Algeria. It is the standard marinade for grilled fish in Moroccan coastal cities like Essaouira, Agadir, and Casablanca. The same paste is used on grilled whole sardines, stuffed bream, and baked sea bass. It keeps well in the fridge and works as a sauce or dipping paste as well as a marinade.
